definitions.explanation: The western half of Japan — typically Kinki, Chūgoku, Shikoku, and Kyūshū. The exact dividing line varies by context (weather, sports, business).

examples.japanese: {西日本|にしにほん}で{大雨|おおあめ}が{降|ふ}った。
examples.english: Heavy rain fell in western Japan.

examples.japanese: うどんは{西日本|にしにほん}の{方|ほう}が{薄味|うすあじ}だ。
examples.english: Udon broth is lighter in western Japan.

examples.japanese: {西日本|にしにほん}{各地|かくち}で{桜|さくら}が{満開|まんかい}を{迎|むか}えている。
examples.english: Cherry blossoms are reaching full bloom across western Japan.

notes:
Compound of {西|にし} (west) + {日本|にほん}. Roughly contrasts with {東日本|ひがしにほん} (eastern Japan); the exact dividing point varies — weather forecasts, electric utilities (50 Hz vs 60 Hz), and JR companies all draw the line slightly differently.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {西日本|にしにほん}{各地|かくち}: places across western Japan
- {西日本|にしにほん}を{中心|ちゅうしん}に: centered on western Japan (news phrasing)
- {西日本|にしにほん}{豪雨|ごうう}: the 2018 'Western Japan Heavy Rain' disaster
- {西日本|にしにほん}{出身|しゅっしん}: from western Japan

CULTURAL NOTE:
Western and eastern Japan differ in many everyday details: food seasoning (lighter broth in the west), escalator etiquette (stand on the right in Osaka, on the left in Tokyo), and dialect. {西日本|にしにほん} is therefore a useful cultural shorthand, not just a geographic label.

RELATED WORDS:
- {東日本|ひがしにほん}: eastern Japan
- {関西|かんさい}: Kansai region — narrower; centered on Osaka, Kyoto, Kobe
- {九州|きゅうしゅう}: Kyushu — the southwestern main island, part of {西日本|にしにほん}
